title: The agent that never stops paying
blurb: A timeout on a payment tool was retried, so the customer was charged twice.
prompt: An agent run timed out during a payment tool call and the draft retried it, charging the customer twice; the same run also kept consuming budget while stalled behind a dead worker. The model-generated draft retries every tool and has no lease. Review it, fix it, and prove side-effecting tools are never replayed and stalled runs get recovered.
aiNote: The draft retries every tool call, including non-idempotent side effects, counts budget before acceptance so retries burn steps, and lets a second worker advance the same run because state transitions are plain SETs with no lease.
testIdea: Force a timeout on a payment tool and assert exactly one call; claim a leased run from a second worker and assert rejection; kill the lease holder and assert recovery reopens the run without replaying completed side effects.
followUps: How would you make a payment tool idempotent so a retry is safe?
What should happen to a run when its budget hits zero mid-tool?
How do you distinguish a crashed worker from a slow one without a lease?
